passages.text: Simon said, “What then? Does that which is lifeless have the natural capacity to produce bad and good things?” Peter said, “On this account it is neither good nor bad, because it does not act by choice, being lifeless and insensible. Therefore here too one can discern how, though lifeless, it brings forth living things, and though insensible, it appears to fashion skillfully formed shapes of both animals and plants.” Simon said, “What then? If God himself animated it, is he not himself the cause of the bad things it brings forth?” Peter said, “If God animated it according to his own will, his spirit works on it, and there is no longer anything hostile to God, equal in power to him, or impossible for him, because everything he brings about comes about as he wills. But you will say, ‘He himself is the cause of evil, if he himself works bad things through it.’ What, then, will you call the bad things? Venomous creeping creatures and deadly herbs, or demons, or also some other things capable of troubling human beings? These—the ..... fine things—would not have existed if the human being had not sinned, on account of which death entered. For while the human being was ......, the venom of creeping creatures was not at work, nor the effects of bad herbs; disturbances by demons did not occur, nor did any other affliction have the natural capacity to attach itself to him. But through sin he fell away from being immortal and has, as I said, become susceptible to every affliction. But if you say, ‘Why, then, did human nature originally come into being susceptible to death?’ I tell you: because of freedom of choice. For if we were not susceptible to death, as immortals we could not be punished for a sin committed with freedom of choice. Thus, because of a somewhat greater immunity to suffering, even if we were bad by choice, justice too would be weakened, since those with bad choices could not be punished because of immunity to suffering.”

lexical_decisions.source_quote: ἡ ἄψυχος οὖσα φύσιν ἔχει ἐμφύειν τὰ κακὰ καὶ τὰ ἀγαθά;
lexical_decisions.chosen: Does that which is lifeless have the natural capacity to produce bad and good things?
lexical_decisions.rationale: The feminine subject is not independently named in this supplied section, so that which is lifeless preserves it without introducing an unprinted matter noun. φύσιν ἔχει expresses a natural capacity or constitution, distinct from moral choice. Produce renders engender or cause to grow.

lexical_decisions.chosen: though lifeless, it brings forth living things
lexical_decisions.rationale: Preserves the repeated lifeless/living contrast; literally without soul versus things possessing soul or animate things. The main text does not turn absence of sensory life into absence of every productive capacity.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: οὐκ αὐτὸς αἴτιός ἐστιν ὧν αὕτη τίκτει κακῶν;
lexical_decisions.chosen: is he not himself the cause of the bad things it brings forth?
lexical_decisions.rationale: The corrected ὧν is a genitive plural relative linking the bad things to what it produces, with its genitive attracted to κακῶν governed by cause of. It is not the participle being. Cause preserves the causal claim, rather than replacing it with a conclusion about guilt.

God’s spirit is the expressed agent working on the previously lifeless subject. The clause is conditional on God having animated it according to his will; it is not an independently asserted account of how every bad thing arises.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: οὐκέτι τῷ θεῷ ἐχθρόν τι ἐστιν ἢ ἰσοδύναμον ἢ ἀδύνατον
lexical_decisions.chosen: there is no longer anything hostile to God, equal in power to him, or impossible for him
lexical_decisions.rationale: The dative God is understood with the coordinated predicates: hostile to him, equal in power to him, or impossible for him. Impossible represents a limit on capability, not moral opposition; the subsequent everything as he wills supports this reading. Powerless is another lexical sense of ἀδύνατον if read as an intrinsic predicate of the thing, but would not give the same shared-dative argument.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: ἅπερ τὰ ..... λεπτὰ οὐκ ἂν ἦν
lexical_decisions.chosen: These—the ..... fine things—would not have existed
lexical_decisions.rationale: Exactly five printed dots remain before fine. λεπτά can mean fine, subtle, thin, or small; fine here is not a commendation of moral goodness. The gap prevents identifying any missing qualification or more precise category; none is restored.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: οὗ εἵνεκεν θάνατος παρεισῆλθε...... γὰρ ὄντος τοῦ ἀνθρώπου
lexical_decisions.chosen: on account of which death entered. For while the human being was ......
lexical_decisions.rationale: On account of which takes the preceding sin event as the causal antecedent, supported by through sin later in the section. On whose account, referring to the human being, is another possible relative attachment. The six-dot gap is retained as the unspecified state associated with the ensuing being-clause; English places the visible gap after was rather than restoring an adjective or any lost words before the Greek γάρ.

As in the opening question, φύσιν ἔχει concerns natural capacity, not choice or intention. The main text keeps the claim that afflictions did not have capacity to attach to him, rather than saying only that they happened not to do so.

αὐτεξούσιον is being in one’s own power or self-determination, here the reason susceptibility to death permits accountability. The distinction between freely chosen sin and mere natural production remains.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: καὶ οὕτως διὰ τὸ ἀπαθὲς πλεῖόν τι, κἂν τῇ προαιρέσει ἦμεν κακοί, ἡ καὶ δικαιοσύνη ἐξησθένει
lexical_decisions.chosen: Thus, because of a somewhat greater immunity to suffering, even if we were bad by choice, justice too would be weakened
lexical_decisions.rationale: The main text attaches πλεῖόν τι to immunity to suffering, preferring its immediate placement after τὸ ἀπαθές within the cause phrase, before the intervening even-if clause. The preceding contrast between hypothesized immortals and death-susceptible beings supports reading a greater degree of immunity. The indefinite τι is represented by somewhat. A materially different attachment takes πλεῖόν τι adverbially with ἐξησθένει across the intervening clause: Thus, because of immunity to suffering, even if we were bad by choice, justice too would be weakened somewhat more. That reading places the degree on weakening justice rather than on immunity. The printed comma does not uniquely settle the attachment. Something more in the immunity to suffering is a more literal version of the main attachment, not a substitute for disclosing this adverbial alternative; no additional agency, privilege, or restored Greek is asserted.

source_issues.issue: The former selected transcription read ὢν, being, but the independently blind-checked print crop now reads ὧν with rough breathing and circumflex. This is a documented print-transcription correction, not a grammatical conjecture. The blind receipt notes that the breathing/circumflex strokes are crowded and partly merged, with the breathing contour less distinct; that ink uncertainty remains disclosed. The main text uses the selected relative reading and does not certify each crowded stroke as perfectly clear.

The selected edition prints exactly five dots before λεπτά. Exactly five remain in English, without filling the lost qualification or substituting a complete reconstructed phrase. Fine is a rendering of the surviving adjective, with subtle, thin, or small as lexical alternatives.

source_issues.source_quote: θάνατος παρεισῆλθε...... γὰρ ὄντος τοῦ ἀνθρώπου
source_issues.issue: The selected edition prints exactly six dots between death entered and for ... the human being being. Exactly six remain in English, moved to the open complement position after was to keep the surviving being-clause readable without identifying its missing qualification. No immortal or other adjective is restored from the later explicit immortality statement. An alternative retaining the physical interruption order is death entered ...... For while the human being existed, but that bare existential English risks obscuring the missing state. The main reading makes the unresolved state visible, not recovered.
